facts.material: unidentified active ingredient (acid-suppressing drug subject of an FDA NDA for NERD, erosive esophagitis healing and maintenance; possibly a potassium-competitive acid blocker such as vonoprazan or tegoprazan)
facts.function: therapeutic treatment of acid-related digestive disorders
facts.form: not stated (assumed finished dosage form, e.g., tablets)

gri_path: GRI 1: if imported in measured doses or retail packings, heading 3004 medicaments; if in bulk, chapter 29 (heterocyclic compound) or 3003

GRI 6: Medicaments primarily affecting the digestive system: no specific line for this active ingredient (pantoprazole, famotidine, ondansetron, glycopyrrolate, loperamide lines do not apply), so 'Other' .60

rejected_alternatives.reason: bulk active ingredient with N- and O-heterocycles (e.g., tegoprazan) would go here if imported in bulk; form not stated
bulk vonoprazan (a sulfonamide) would go here if imported in bulk; form not stated
pantoprazole line; no indication the drug is pantoprazole

missing_facts: What is the active ingredient (name/CAS number)?
Is it imported in bulk or in finished dosage form (tablets, capsules), and in what packaging?
classification.rationale: The description gives only the NDA indications (NERD, erosive esophagitis healing and maintenance), not the product, its active ingredient or its form. Assuming a finished dosage-form medicament for acid-related digestive disease, it falls in heading 3004, subheading 3004.90.92, under the digestive-system 'Other' line 3004.90.92.60, as CBP did for lansoprazole tablets in NY N323546. If the active ingredient is imported in bulk, it would instead be a chapter 29 heterocyclic or sulfonamide compound.
